result.title: ViRA: Toward Ultra-High-Resolution Visual Agents via Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization
result.summary: Visual agents answer questions about ultra-high-resolution photos by zooming into the relevant regions. However, existing agents often answer from common sense instead of reading the evidence. Reinforcement learning (RL) on the final answer cannot correct this, because a guess earns the same reward as reading. We propose Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization (CrossRPO), which trains agents on contrast sets. A contrast set asks one question about several versions of an image that differ only in a small region with the evidence and have different answers, so only reading the evidence solves the whole set. CrossRPO rewards solving the whole set, and we prove that it does not reinforce a set answered from common sense. We build contrast sets for training (ViRA-Train) and evaluation (ViRA-Bench) by editing one small object in images of 21 to 120 megapixels, and we photograph further sets with real changes (ViRA-Bench-Real) to exclude editing traces. We train two Visual Reasoning Agents, ViRA-9B and ViRA-27B, with CrossRPO on only about 3,500 items of ViRA-Train each. CrossRPO achieves 63.3% set accuracy on ViRA-Bench at the maximum resolution, against 59.3% for GRPO. ViRA-9B is the most accurate open model of its size on all benchmarks, and ViRA-27B outperforms Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6-Luna, both at their highest thinking level, on most benchmarks.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization（CrossRPO），用仅在某一小区域不同、答案各异的对比图像集训练超高分辨率视觉 agent，使其必须放大读取证据而非依赖常识作答，并构建 21–120 百万像素的训练集、编辑式评测集与真实拍摄评测集。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应「LOOK」阶段的证据获取与奖励分配问题：集级对比奖励可抑制凭先验猜测，其对比集构造方式可供核查 agent 是否真正使用所获视觉证据，以及如何为视觉证据筛选设计监督。
